analysis: MLX lazy evaluation fuses the host loop's B*S slice_updates into fewer GPU passes than the naive B*S pool copies, so the host loop is not as catastrophic as the op count suggests.
Native path is consistently faster (1.25-1.31x best, ~2x mean) and deterministic: exactly one pool copy + one scatter launch, independent of lazy-fusion behavior and Python loop overhead.
Dominant residual cost is the full-pool copy; removing it requires an in-place scatter ABI (out= aliasing input), which the tvm_ffi owner-output contract currently does not express.
